policies.name: Deny write to removable disks
policies.summary: Blocks writing to USB and other removable disks. Read can still succeed. This is the Storage CSP, not Defender device control.
policies.intunePath: Devices > Configuration > Custom, or Settings catalog > Storage
policies.note: 0 allows writes (default). Does not stop execution or read. Pair with device control if you need allow-lists.

policies.name: Deny read, write, and execute on removable disks
policies.summary: Administrative template set that closes read and execute, which the Storage write-deny setting does not cover.
policies.intunePath: Settings catalog > Administrative Templates > System > Removable Storage Access
policies.note: Also set RemovableDisks: Deny write access and RemovableDisks: Deny execute access in the same template folder. Prefer this catalog over hand-built XML when you do not need a hardware allow-list.

policies.name: Turn off AutoPlay for every drive
policies.summary: Stops the shell from offering to play or run content when a volume mounts. A removable-disk write deny does not do this.
policies.intunePath: Settings catalog > Administrative Templates > Windows Components > AutoPlay Policies
policies.note: ADMX-backed, so the value is an ADMX string, not an integer. Autorun_Box 255 turns AutoPlay off for all drives; 181 covers CD-ROM and removable media only. Teams that only set Storage deny-write still get an AutoPlay prompt for content that was already on the disk.

policies.name: Do not execute AutoRun commands
policies.summary: Default AutoRun behavior. NoAutorun_Dropdown 1 refuses to run autorun.inf commands.
policies.intunePath: Settings catalog > Administrative Templates > Windows Components > AutoPlay Policies
policies.note: ADMX-backed String value. NoAutorun_Dropdown: 1 = do not execute any autorun commands, 2 = automatically execute autorun commands. Pair it with TurnOffAutoPlay.

policies.name: Disallow AutoPlay for phones and cameras
policies.summary: Closes the AutoPlay prompt for MTP and other devices that never mount as a disk. Device control still has to cover WpdDevices if you want a real block.
policies.intunePath: Settings catalog > Administrative Templates > Windows Components > AutoPlay Policies
policies.note: ADMX-backed String value with no data elements: <enabled/> turns the restriction on, <disabled/> turns it off. This does not replace Defender device control for Windows portable devices.

policies.name: Deny file-system write, not only disk write
policies.summary: Encrypted USB often needs a disk-level write to unlock, then copies files at the file-system layer. A disk-level deny blocks the unlock. A file-system write deny blocks the copy and still lets the drive mount.
policies.intunePath: Endpoint security > Attack surface reduction > Device control > Removable storage
policies.omaUri: Device control access mask. Not a single integer CSP.
policies.value: Deny Write on File system for RemovableMediaDevices. Allow Read.
policies.note: The device control FAQ calls this out: creating an empty folder is not a file write, some Kingston drives need Execute on their virtual CD, and some WD drives need disk-level write to unlock. Read the DeviceEvents access mask in advanced hunting before you treat a block as a product bug.

policies.name: Enable Defender device control
policies.summary: Turns on Microsoft Defender device control so removable media, WPD, CD/DVD, and printers can be allow-listed or denied.
policies.intunePath: Endpoint security > Attack surface reduction > Device control
policies.note: 0 disables. Endpoint security profiles are preferred. Use this OMA-URI when you must ship a custom profile.

policies.name: Device control default enforcement
policies.summary: Decision when no device-control rule matches. Deny is the lockdown posture for USB. Intune's device control UI cannot set this; the OMA-URI can.
policies.intunePath: Devices > Configuration > Custom
policies.note: 1 = Allow (default), 2 = Deny. If you set Deny, ship an Allow rule for approved media or you will block every secured device.

policies.name: Secured device families
policies.summary: Primary IDs that device control protects. RemovableMediaDevices is the USB storage family.
policies.intunePath: Devices > Configuration > Custom
policies.note: Allowed tokens: RemovableMediaDevices, CdRomDevices, WpdDevices, PrinterDevices. Separate with a pipe and no spaces. Add printer or CD only if you mean to control them.

policies.name: Require device encryption
policies.summary: Silent BitLocker enablement for OS volumes that meet the hardware bar (TPM on modern Windows).
policies.intunePath: Endpoint security > Disk encryption > BitLocker
policies.note: Servers: confirm a TPM and that recovery passwords escrow to Entra ID before broad assignment. Server Core has no BitLocker wizard.

policies.name: Encryption method XTS-AES 256
policies.summary: Sets the cipher separately for OS, fixed, and removable drives. XTS-AES 256 for OS and fixed drives; AES-CBC 256 for removable drives so they still open on older Windows.
policies.intunePath: Endpoint security > Disk encryption > BitLocker
policies.note: ADMX-style String value. Method values: 3 AES-CBC 128, 4 AES-CBC 256, 6 XTS-AES 128, 7 XTS-AES 256. Use 7 for removable drives too if every reader runs Windows 10 1511 or later.

policies.name: Require BitLocker on removable drives
policies.summary: Forces encryption before a user can write to a removable drive. Complements USB device control.
policies.intunePath: Endpoint security > Disk encryption > BitLocker > Removable data drives
policies.note: ADMX-style String value. RDVCrossOrg 1 also blocks write access to drives that another organization encrypted; 0 does not. Configure RemovableDrivesConfigureBDE so users can encrypt removable media.

policies.name: Escrow OS drive recovery to Entra
policies.summary: Stores the 48-digit recovery password in the device object. Do not deploy silent encryption without this.
policies.intunePath: Endpoint security > Disk encryption > BitLocker > OS drive recovery
policies.value: <enabled/><data id="OSAllowDRA_Name" value="false"/><data id="OSRecoveryPasswordUsageDropDown_Name" value="2"/><data id="OSRecoveryKeyUsageDropDown_Name" value="2"/><data id="OSHideRecoveryPage_Name" value="true"/><data id="OSActiveDirectoryBackup_Name" value="true"/><data id="OSActiveDirectoryBackupDropDown_Name" value="1"/><data id="OSRequireActiveDirectoryBackup_Name" value="true"/>
policies.note: ADMX-style String value. OSRecoveryPasswordUsageDropDown_Name and OSRecoveryKeyUsageDropDown_Name: 2 allow, 1 require, 0 do not allow. OSActiveDirectoryBackupDropDown_Name 1 backs up the recovery password and key package. OSRequireActiveDirectoryBackup_Name true stops encryption until the key is escrowed to Entra ID or AD DS. The Endpoint security disk encryption profile builds this string for you.

policies.name: Firewall on for domain, private, and public
policies.summary: Enables Windows Firewall on every profile. Public inbound default should stay Block.
policies.intunePath: Endpoint security > Firewall
policies.note: Set all three paths. Set PublicProfile/DefaultInboundAction to 1 (block) and keep outbound allowed unless a server workload needs default-deny egress.

policies.name: Stop local firewall rules from merging
policies.summary: When Intune should win, disable local policy merge so a local admin cannot add an allow rule underneath the MDM policy.
policies.intunePath: Endpoint security > Firewall > Policy settings
policies.note: Set all three paths. Log dropped packets (EnableLogDroppedPackets true) on servers so blocked C2 attempts are visible.

policies.name: Network protection in block mode
policies.summary: Blocks outbound connections to low-reputation hosts, including malware command-and-control, using Microsoft Defender SmartScreen reputation and custom indicators.
policies.intunePath: Endpoint security > Antivirus, or Attack surface reduction
policies.note: 0 off, 1 block, 2 audit. Block mode is required before web content filtering will enforce. Audit first on line-of-business servers.

policies.name: Cloud-delivered protection
policies.summary: Required companion. Network protection, web protection, and block-at-first-sight do nothing useful with the cloud off.
policies.intunePath: Endpoint security > Antivirus
policies.note: 0 disabled, 1 enabled. Pair with CloudBlockLevel.

policies.name: Cloud block level High
policies.summary: How aggressive cloud heuristics are when a file has not been seen before.
policies.intunePath: Endpoint security > Antivirus
policies.note: 0 Default, 2 High, 4 High+, 6 Zero tolerance. High is the usual enterprise baseline. Zero tolerance will block unknown files and needs an exception process.

policies.name: Custom network indicators for C2
policies.summary: IP, domain, and URL indicators maintained in the Defender portal. Block indicators are how you add a specific C2 that reputation has not classified yet.
policies.intunePath: Microsoft Defender portal > Settings > Endpoints > Indicators
policies.omaUri: Not an OMA-URI — Defender portal indicators, enforced by network protection
policies.value: Action: Block execution. Enable NetworkProtection in block mode and file hash computation.
policies.note: Certificate indicators are a separate list. Network indicators on Windows Server need network protection in block mode and the device onboarded to Defender for Endpoint.

policies.name: File hash computation
policies.summary: Lets custom file indicators and some investigations match samples by hash.
policies.intunePath: Endpoint security > Antivirus

policies.name: Web content filtering
policies.summary: Category filtering (adult, legal liability, leisure, high bandwidth, uncategorized, and the rest of the Defender category set). Configured in the Defender portal, not as an OMA-URI.
policies.intunePath: Defender portal > Settings > Endpoints > Web content filtering
policies.value: Create a policy, pick blocked categories, scope the device group.
policies.note: Windows 11 and Windows Server 2019 or later, onboarded to Defender for Endpoint. Malware and phishing sites are blocked by network protection even when a category policy is not assigned.

policies.name: Potentially unwanted application protection
policies.summary: Blocks PUAs in the browser and on disk. Part of the web protection stack alongside SmartScreen.
policies.intunePath: Endpoint security > Antivirus
policies.note: 0 off, 1 block, 2 audit.

policies.name: Windows shell SmartScreen
policies.summary: Reputation check when a user runs a downloaded file from Explorer.
policies.intunePath: Settings catalog > SmartScreen
policies.note: Also set SmartScreen/PreventOverrideForFilesInShell to 1 so users cannot click through. Server Core has no shell; this setting matters on Windows 11 and Server with Desktop Experience.

policies.name: Edge Defender SmartScreen
policies.summary: Turns on Microsoft Defender SmartScreen inside Chromium Edge, including site and download prompts.
policies.intunePath: Settings catalog > Microsoft Edge > SmartScreen settings
policies.note: Settings catalog is preferred. The ADMX prefix changes if an older Edge ADMX ingest is used. Edge is not installed by default on Server Core.

policies.name: Edge SmartScreen block potentially unwanted apps
policies.summary: Edge-side PUA blocking. Independent of Defender PUAProtection and worth setting both.
policies.intunePath: Settings catalog > Microsoft Edge > SmartScreen settings

policies.name: Edge prevent SmartScreen bypass
policies.summary: Users cannot continue to a site or open a file that SmartScreen blocked.
policies.intunePath: Settings catalog > Microsoft Edge > SmartScreen settings
policies.note: Also enable PreventSmartScreenPromptOverrideForFiles with value <enabled/>.

policies.name: App Control for Business policy
policies.summary: Deploys a signed WDAC policy (.cip) through the ApplicationControl CSP. This is the supported application control stack for new designs.
policies.intunePath: Endpoint security > App Control for Business
policies.value: Base64 of the signed binary policy (.cip / .p7b)
policies.note: Start from Microsoft recommended block rules plus the recommended driver block rules, in audit, then enforce. Managed installer and Intelligent Security Graph (option 14) are supplemental. Each base or supplemental policy is its own PolicyId node.

policies.name: AppLocker EXE collection
policies.summary: Legacy application control. Still valid for per-user rules. Microsoft no longer invests in new AppLocker features; prefer App Control for Business.
policies.intunePath: Devices > Configuration > Custom
policies.value: AppLocker RuleCollection XML for Type=Exe, EnforcementMode Enabled or AuditOnly
policies.note: Repeat for MSI, Script, StoreApps, and DLL. DLL rules have a measurable performance cost — leave them off unless you have a specific need. Paste plain XML in Intune, not escaped XML. The AppLocker service must be running.

policies.name: Pilot ring: engine updates channel = Current Channel (Staged)
policies.summary: Pilot devices get each release in the staged wave, ahead of the fleet. This is the supported way to stage Defender updates.
policies.intunePath: Endpoint security > Antivirus > Microsoft Defender Antivirus (Settings catalog: Defender > Update channels)
policies.note: Values: 0 Not configured (default: Microsoft paces the device in the gradual rollout), 2 Beta Channel, 3 Current Channel (Preview), 4 Current Channel (Staged), 5 Current Channel (Broad), 6 Critical: Time delay. Assign Staged and Broad to different groups.

policies.name: Broad fleet: engine updates channel = Current Channel (Broad)
policies.summary: The rest of the fleet waits for the broad wave, after the staged wave has had time to surface problems.
policies.intunePath: Endpoint security > Antivirus > Microsoft Defender Antivirus (Settings catalog: Defender > Update channels)
policies.note: Values: 0 Not configured (default: Microsoft paces the device in the gradual rollout), 2 Beta Channel, 3 Current Channel (Preview), 4 Current Channel (Staged), 5 Current Channel (Broad), 6 Critical: Time delay. Assign Staged and Broad to different groups.

policies.name: Pilot ring: platform updates channel = Current Channel (Staged)
policies.summary: Pilot devices get each release in the staged wave, ahead of the fleet. This is the supported way to stage Defender updates.
policies.intunePath: Endpoint security > Antivirus > Microsoft Defender Antivirus (Settings catalog: Defender > Update channels)
policies.note: Values: 0 Not configured (default), 2 Beta Channel, 3 Current Channel (Preview), 4 Current Channel (Staged), 5 Current Channel (Broad), 6 Critical: Time delay. Assign Staged and Broad to different groups.

policies.name: Broad fleet: platform updates channel = Current Channel (Broad)
policies.summary: The rest of the fleet waits for the broad wave, after the staged wave has had time to surface problems.
policies.intunePath: Endpoint security > Antivirus > Microsoft Defender Antivirus (Settings catalog: Defender > Update channels)
policies.note: Values: 0 Not configured (default), 2 Beta Channel, 3 Current Channel (Preview), 4 Current Channel (Staged), 5 Current Channel (Broad), 6 Critical: Time delay. Assign Staged and Broad to different groups.

policies.name: Pilot ring: security intelligence updates channel = Current Channel (Staged)
policies.summary: Pilot devices get each release in the staged wave, ahead of the fleet. This is the supported way to stage Defender updates.
policies.intunePath: Endpoint security > Antivirus > Microsoft Defender Antivirus (Settings catalog: Defender > Update channels)
policies.note: Values: 0 Not configured (default), 4 Current Channel (Staged), 5 Current Channel (Broad). Assign Staged and Broad to different groups.

policies.name: Broad fleet: security intelligence updates channel = Current Channel (Broad)
policies.summary: The rest of the fleet waits for the broad wave, after the staged wave has had time to surface problems.
policies.intunePath: Endpoint security > Antivirus > Microsoft Defender Antivirus (Settings catalog: Defender > Update channels)
policies.note: Values: 0 Not configured (default), 4 Current Channel (Staged), 5 Current Channel (Broad). Assign Staged and Broad to different groups.

policies.name: Broad ring checks signatures every 4 hours
policies.summary: Hourly checks (value 1) take a faulty security intelligence push in the same hour it is published. Keep 1 on a small pilot ring. Keep the rest of the fleet at 4 so you have time to hold the update.
policies.intunePath: Endpoint security > Antivirus > Security intelligence updates
policies.note: 0 disables checks. 1 is every hour. 8 is the CSP default. Do not assign 1 to every device. Assign 1 only to a pilot group that can tolerate a bad detection for an hour. This is an extra option on top of update channels, not the main way to stage updates.

policies.name: Pilot ring checks signatures every hour
policies.summary: The canary for mpam-fe.exe. These devices take the hourly Microsoft update first. Watch their alerts before the broad ring is allowed to move.
policies.intunePath: Endpoint security > Antivirus > Security intelligence updates
policies.note: Same OMA-URI as the broad ring. Scope it to a different group. If the pilot starts quarantining good files, do not let the broad ring's 4-hour check run until Microsoft ships a higher signature version or you publish a revision yourself. This is an extra option on top of update channels, not the main way to stage updates.

policies.name: Broad ring: internal update server first
policies.summary: WSUS or Configuration Manager can decline KB2267602 while you confirm a signature. The cloud (MMPC) stays last, so a bad hourly package is not pulled the moment Windows Update fails.
policies.intunePath: Endpoint security > Antivirus > Security intelligence updates
policies.note: Tokens, in an order you choose: InternalDefinitionUpdateServer, MicrosoftUpdateServer, MMPC, FileShares. No spaces. If WSUS does not approve security intelligence, devices follow this list and will still reach MMPC. That is what you want for availability, and what you must pause during a bad push.

policies.name: Pilot ring: Microsoft cloud first
policies.summary: Pilot devices skip the internal approval queue and take the public mpam-fe.exe. That is how you see a bad hourly package before everyone else.
policies.intunePath: Endpoint security > Antivirus > Security intelligence updates
policies.note: Different assignment from the broad-ring order. MMPC is the definitionupdates.microsoft.com channel this page polls.

policies.name: Emergency file share for a revised package
policies.summary: During a bad push, put the corrected mpam-fe.exe on a share you control and move FileShares to the front of the fallback order. Remove that override after the public package is good again.
policies.intunePath: Endpoint security > Antivirus > Security intelligence updates
policies.note: Replace the UNC with your share. Pipe-separate more than one. The share must contain the architecture-correct package. Point fallback at FileShares only for the incident, or the fleet will stop taking Microsoft's later revisions.

policies.name: Incident only: allow (ignore) Low and Moderate threats
policies.summary: During a confirmed false-positive incident, Low and Moderate detections are allowed instead of remediated, so a faulty signature quarantines less. High and Severe are still quarantined.
policies.intunePath: Endpoint security > Antivirus > Remediation
policies.note: Format is threat-level=action pairs separated by |. Levels: 1 Low, 2 Moderate, 4 High, 5 Severe. Actions: 1 Clean, 2 Quarantine, 3 Remove, 6 Allow, 8 User defined, 10 Block. Steady state: 1=2|2=2|4=2|5=2. Allow does not restore files already quarantined and does not suppress alerts. Pair it with an Allow indicator.
policies.warning: This lets real Low and Moderate threats run. Remove it as soon as Microsoft ships a corrected signature, and never leave it in a baseline.

policies.name: Drop cloud block level while a cloud detection is faulty
policies.summary: If the harm is block-at-first-sight or a High+ cloud heuristic, set the cloud block level back to Default until the intelligence revision lands. The steady state on this page is High (2), not Default.
policies.intunePath: Endpoint security > Antivirus
policies.note: 0 Default, 2 High, 4 High+, 6 Zero tolerance. Assign 0 only to the ring that is blocking good files, and remove the assignment when the pilot is clean on the revised signature. Do not leave Zero tolerance in place while you are chasing a false positive.

policies.name: Keep sending safe samples so Microsoft can revise
policies.summary: A faulty signature gets a revised mpam-fe faster when Microsoft has the sample. Turning sample submission off during the incident slows that revision.
policies.intunePath: Endpoint security > Antivirus, or Endpoint detection and response
policies.note: 0 always prompt, 1 send safe samples automatically, 2 never send, 3 send all samples automatically. Use 1 on servers. Use 3 only on a lab device that holds the false-positive file and no sensitive data.

policies.name: Allow indicator for the file that was wrongly detected
policies.summary: Stops Defender from blocking that hash, and stops automated investigation from treating it as malicious. This is the portal control. It is not an exclusion for the sensor.
policies.intunePath: security.microsoft.com > Settings > Endpoints > Indicators > File hashes
policies.omaUri: Not an OMA-URI. Defender portal indicator, action Allow.
policies.value: Allow the affected file hash or your publisher certificate. Do not allow MsSense.exe or SenseIR.exe.
policies.note: An Allow indicator does not restore files already quarantined; release those from the quarantine on the device or in the portal. Scope it to a device group if you can. Remove it after the revised signature is on the fleet and a rescan is clean.

policies.name: Suppress the false-positive alert
policies.summary: Hides the repeat alert in security.microsoft.com. Suppression does not stop quarantine or a block. Use it with the Allow indicator, not instead of it.
policies.intunePath: security.microsoft.com > Settings > Endpoints > Rules > Alert suppression
policies.omaUri: Not an OMA-URI. Created from the alert at security.microsoft.com/alerts.
policies.value: Create suppression rule from the alert. Scope to the detection title and a device group. Set an end date.
policies.note: Classify the alert as False positive first, then suppress. If a SIEM also ingests the alert, suppress it there too or the queue just moves.

policies.name: Onboard the Sense service from Intune
policies.summary: MsSense.exe (service name Sense) only reports after the tenant onboarding blob is applied. Impaired communications and no sensor data are both useless until that blob is on the device.
policies.intunePath: Endpoint security > Endpoint detection and response > Windows
policies.omaUri: Tenant onboarding blob. Do not hand-write it.
policies.value: Package type: Onboarding. Blob downloaded from security.microsoft.com > Settings > Endpoints > Onboarding.
policies.note: Intune shows the sensor count under Endpoint security > Overview. Offboarding packages expire; download a fresh one. Sample sharing and expedited telemetry are on the same profile and can stay at their defaults unless a vendor health notice says otherwise.

asr.name: Block abuse of exploited vulnerable signed drivers
Block persistence through WMI event subscription
asr.note: Not configurable in Configuration Manager. Intune and CSP only.

asr.name: Block executable content from email client and webmail
Block all Office applications from creating child processes
Block Office applications from creating executable content
Block Office applications from injecting code into other processes
Block Win32 API calls from Office macros
asr.note: Client Office feature. Not applicable on Windows Server without Office.

asr.name: Block Office communication apps from creating child processes
Block JavaScript or VBScript from launching downloaded executable content
Block execution of potentially obfuscated scripts
Block executable files unless they meet prevalence, age, or trusted list
asr.note: High business impact. Stay in audit until you have reviewed blocks.

asr.name: Block untrusted and unsigned processes that run from USB
Block process creations originating from PSExec and WMI commands
asr.note: Breaks many admin and management tools. Audit, then exclude the management hosts.

asr.name: Block Adobe Reader from creating child processes
Block rebooting machine in Safe Mode
Block use of copied or impersonated system tools
Block Webshell creation for Servers
asr.note: Applies to Windows Server running the Exchange role, not to a general file server. Leave Not Configured in Group Policy if Defender security settings management owns it.

features.name: Security intelligence channel
features.summary: Detection content ships several times a day as KB2267602. Engine updates ride along about monthly. Platform updates are a separate package and stay supported back to N-2.

features.name: Sense sensor and SenseIR
features.summary: The EDR sensor is MsSense.exe, service name Sense. Live response and automated investigation start SenseIR.exe, which often launches PowerShell as SYSTEM. Health for both is in the Defender portal sensor report, not in the antivirus signature version.

features.name: USB layers a write-deny does not cover
features.summary: Removable-disk write deny leaves read, execute, AutoPlay, AutoRun, and MTP phones alone. Encrypted sticks often need disk-level write to unlock and a file-system write deny to stop the copy. This page lists those controls next to device control and the USB ASR rule.

features.name: Attack surface reduction rules
features.summary: Behavioral blocks for Office, scripts, USB, LSASS, drivers, and WMI. Standard protection rules are meant to be in block mode. The rest should be audited before they are enforced. Not available on Linux or macOS.

features.name: Device control
features.summary: Allow or deny removable storage, Windows portable devices, CD/DVD, and printers, with per-device exceptions. Default enforcement is an OMA-URI, not a toggle in the Intune rule builder.

features.name: Network protection
features.summary: Outbound block or audit against Microsoft's URL and IP reputation, which covers a large share of commodity C2. Custom indicators extend it. Still listed as preview on Linux, which is out of scope here.

features.name: Web content filtering
features.summary: Category policies in the Defender portal. Enforcement depends on network protection in block mode and an onboarded Defender for Endpoint sensor.

features.name: Web protection
features.summary: The combination of network protection, SmartScreen, custom indicators, and web content filtering. Report location is the Defender portal Web protection page.

features.name: SmartScreen and Edge
features.summary: Shell reputation for downloaded programs, plus Edge site, download, and PUA checks. Bypass can be removed by policy on both surfaces.

features.name: App Control for Business
features.summary: WDAC policies deployed from Intune, including Microsoft recommended block and driver block rules. Prefer this over AppLocker for new allow-listing.

features.name: Tamper protection
features.summary: Stops local changes to core Defender settings. Turn it on in the Antivirus endpoint security profile or from Defender security settings management. There is no general-purpose OMA-URI that replaces that switch.

features.name: Local AI agent discovery
features.summary: Defender inventories supported local AI agents and their MCP servers on onboarded Windows devices, and exposes them in the AI agent inventory and advanced hunting.
features.statusNote: From the Defender for Endpoint what's new page.

features.name: Agent runtime protection in Intune
features.summary: The Defender for Endpoint agent runtime protection template in Intune is generally available, including AI agent runtime inspection.
features.statusNote: Source is a blog or news post. Treat as reported until a Learn page confirms it.

features.name: Microsoft Execution Containers
features.summary: An OS-enforced containment boundary for local AI agents on Windows, so an agent keeps least privilege instead of inheriting the user.
features.statusNote: Source is a blog or news post. Treat as reported until a Learn page confirms it.
